mcqs.question: What's the correct first move when triaging a stale-read complaint?
options: Walk the read path backward from the user's screen to the source of truth, checking each layer in turn
Immediately restart the database to clear any potential staleness
Assume it's replication lag and check replica metrics only
Ask the user to clear their browser cache and close the ticket
mcqs.explanation: Staleness can be introduced at any layer between the user and the database, so a systematic backward walk is what actually finds the cause. Restarting the database is a blind hammer, assuming replication lag skips the cheaper cache checks, and closing the ticket without investigating risks missing a real, recurring bug.

mcqs.question: In the 'profile reverted' example, what actually caused the stale read?
options: Replication lag between the primary and a read replica
A cache-aside race where a concurrent read repopulated the cache with the old value right after the write's invalidation
The database silently rolled back the write
The CDN served a cached page from before the user even made the edit
mcqs.explanation: The write correctly invalidated the cache, but a concurrent read slipped in immediately after and repopulated it with the pre-update value — a cache-aside race, not replication lag, a database rollback, or a CDN issue.

mcqs.question: Why is a layer-by-layer triage script better than guessing from the last incident?
options: It's always faster in absolute time, regardless of the actual cause
It removes the need for any monitoring dashboards
It systematically rules layers out with cheap checks first, instead of risking a long investigation aimed at the wrong layer
It only works for cache-related incidents
mcqs.explanation: The script's value is discipline, not raw speed in every case — it checks cheap things first so you never spend an hour chasing a hunch before ruling out the five-second checks. It doesn't remove the need for dashboards (it often relies on them) and applies to any layer, not just caching.

mcqs.question: What's wrong with assuming every stale-read complaint is caused by replication lag?
options: Replication lag never actually causes stale reads
It means the database needs to be restarted immediately
It's only true for systems that don't use caching at all
Client caches, CDNs, and application caches all sit in front of the database and can serve stale data with no replication involved
mcqs.explanation: Several layers between the user and the database can independently introduce staleness — jumping straight to replicas can burn the whole investigation on a layer that was never at fault. Replication lag is a real cause sometimes, just not the only one, and this has nothing to do with restarting the database.
